title: A Moon City for a Million People? Water Might Run Out
summary:
Could one million people live on the Moon? Two scientists checked the numbers. Their answer is yes, but only for a short time. Power is not the problem. Water is.

SpaceX chief Elon Musk has said his company wants to build a city on the Moon that grows by itself in less than 10 years. A Mars city would take more than 20 years, he said. Blue Origin chief Jeff Bezos has said millions of people will live in space by 2045. Martin Elvis, an astrophysicist at Harvard University's Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory, and Jonathan McDowell, an astrophysicist at Durham University in England, wanted to test those ideas.

In a paper in the journal Frontiers in Space Technologies, they found that solar and nuclear power could support one million people on the Moon. But there is not enough water. If the Moon holds about one billion tonnes of water, a city of one million people could last only about 100 years, and only if 98 percent of the water is recycled, the same rate as on the International Space Station. A town of 10,000 people could last for centuries. But Elvis said the one-billion-tonne guess is probably far too high, perhaps 20 or 30 times too big. So do not start packing just yet.
why_it_matters: It shows why dreaming big still needs careful checking, just like making sure you have enough water before a long trip.

background_read: A city on the Moon would need power, air, food, and water for everyone who lives there.
Power can come from the Sun and from nuclear power, but water is much harder to find on the Moon.
People could reuse almost all their water, the way crews do on the International Space Station, yet even that may not be enough for a very large city.
Article_Structure: WHO: Martin Elvis and Jonathan McDowell, two scientists, and company chiefs Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos.
WHAT: They tested whether a city of one million people could live on the Moon and found that water would run out.
WHY: Because there is not enough water on the Moon, even when almost all of it is recycled.
